clue.text: I am strangely diminished, having no purpose

indicators.note: strangely says the two words I am are to be rearranged into an odd new order

parts.note: something diminished has become less

explanation.surface: Someone feels oddly reduced and without direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished' looks like part of the surface's mood, but it simply supplies the second piece; 'strangely' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless describes drifting along without any goal or intention.

clue.text: Stomach bad — poor sign

indicators.note: poor suggests the word bad is in a poor state and must be rearranged

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A bad stomach is an ill sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly, the part of the body holding the gut.

clue.text: Take car round Ulster to check up

indicators.note: round says the driving word goes around Northern Ireland

parts.note: to motor is to travel by car
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Drive around Northern Ireland to inspect things.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to keep watch over or inspect something regularly.

clue.text: American under tree is senior politician

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the American below the tree

parts.note: the elder is a tree with white flowers and dark berries
an American is cryptically a States man

explanation.surface: An American sitting beneath a tree is an important politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' in a down entry puts the second piece below the tree; 'American' is read as a man from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving, respected politician whose advice carries weight.

clue.text: Feeling enraptured about New Age

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or carried away

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Being thrilled by the New Age movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude towards something.

clue.text: She tempted sailors, absolutely legless

definitions.meaning: a sea maiden of legend luring seafarers
having a fish's tail rather than any legs at all

explanation.surface: A temptress of seafarers who is completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, but here it is literal: a tail where legs would be.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-tailed women of sea legend lured sailors and had no legs.

clue.text: Doctor took fish, a sort of eel

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A doctor caught a fish that looks like an eel.
explanation.definitionFit: The moray is a species of eel living in warm seas.

clue.text: Their turn to let you in

definitions.text: Their turn to let you in

parts.words: Their turn to let you in
parts.note: sounds like taking turns as a gatekeeper, but the entrance literally spins round to admit people

explanation.surface: Someone's turn on door duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' as a go in a rota is the false reading; these entrances physically rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrances with panels rotating on a central axis, common in large buildings.

clue.text: Impossible to persuade a worker to go round barrier

indicators.note: to go round says the article and the worker surround the barrier

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
a dam is a barrier holding back water

explanation.surface: A labourer must detour around a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts the barrier between the article and the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone unshakeable in their opinion.

clue.text: Receiving gun, did swell up

indicators.note: receiving means the word did takes in the gun

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone who got a gun felt puffed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell outward from pressure inside.

clue.text: Brown meets editor in New Zealand port

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Brown has a meeting with an editor in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city with a harbour on the South Island of New Zealand.

clue.text: Discovers amateur in boisterous entertainments

indicators.note: in places the amateur inside the word for rowdy festivities

parts.note: revels are noisy merrymaking parties

explanation.surface: Someone finds an amateur performer at rowdy parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to uncover or expose it, as in discovering a secret.

clue.text: Time off at end of term

definitions.text: Time off at end of term

parts.words: Time off at end of term
parts.note: term here is the term of a pregnancy, not a school term; the holiday comes when a baby is due

explanation.surface: A holiday at the close of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' suggests school, but a pregnancy also runs to term.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid absence from work granted to a mother around the birth of her child.

clue.text: See 11
Customary behaviour when marines are in numbers

indicators.note: are in says the marines sit inside the abbreviation for numbers

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: How people usually act when marines turn up in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are the standard, accepted patterns of conduct in a group.

clue.text: See 3
Endless detail came back, but very thin

indicators.note: came back signals that the run made from both words is read backwards
endless means the word detail loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A tale of detail recalled without end, about someone very thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims DETAIL to DETAI; 'back' reverses DETAI + CAME as one run to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin and wasted, usually through illness or hunger.

clue.text: Song stolen — how help came to Berlin once

definitions.text: how help came to Berlin once

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
lifted is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: A stolen tune and the history of relief to Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1948-49 the Western Allies flew supplies into blockaded West Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies were flown in by aircraft during the Berlin blockade.

clue.text: Testimonial letter

definitions.meaning: a reference vouching for someone's qualities
a single symbol of writing or printing

explanation.definitionFit: A character is both a written reference from an employer and a printed symbol.

clue.text: Retrace movements of food supplier

indicators.note: movements of tells us the letters of retrace shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone retraces where a food supplier went.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides meals for events and functions.

clue.text: In line for a nice piece of chicken?

parts.note: the breast is a choice cut of chicken meat

explanation.surface: Lining up to get a good cut of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level in a row.

clue.text: Start one's day in elaborate clothes

definitions.meaning: to rise from bed in the morning
an outfit, often a showy or odd one

explanation.surface: Someone begins the morning by dressing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise from bed, and a noun for an eye-catching costume or outfit.

clue.text: Prickly choice of national emblem

parts.note: a spiky plant chosen as the symbol of Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: The spiny purple-flowered plant is the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Clown's support going to crumble

definitions.note: read as clown is, the definition with is as a link

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge
to rot is to decay or crumble

explanation.surface: A circus clown's prop is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a sad-faced white clown from French pantomime.

clue.text: Nursery rhyme characters — one may find them incredible

definitions.meaning: the sightless rodents chased by the farmer's wife
a playful gloss: the tale of tails cut with a carving knife is hard to believe

explanation.surface: Some figures from a children's verse that seem unbelievable.
explanation.definitionFit: The trio of sightless rodents in the old children's song chased by a farmer's wife.

clue.text: See 22
Creature like us making attempt to take exercise

indicators.note: to take means the attempt holds the exercise inside

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: An animal resembling us tries to get some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two feet, as do all two-legged animals.

clue.text: See 6
Published car guide that may fold

definitions.text: Published car guide that may fold

parts.words: Published car guide that may fold
parts.note: fold suggests a publication going out of business, but here the printed sheet for drivers is literally folded

explanation.surface: A motoring guide whose publishers might go bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like a business failing; the sheet itself folds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed chart of streets and highways used by drivers, usually folded.

clue.text: Foot of animal, one that moves steadily

definitions.meaning: a pig's foot used as food
a horse or person going at a steady jogging pace

explanation.surface: An animal's foot belongs to something that keeps a steady pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot cooked as food, and also a horse bred for an even gait.

clue.text: Moved back to original pitch to play

definitions.text: Moved back to original pitch to play

parts.words: Moved back to original pitch to play
parts.note: suggests a team returning to its home ground, but means an instrument adjusted to sound right again

explanation.surface: A team went back to its old ground for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a sports field; it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument adjusted again so its notes sound correctly before a performance.

clue.text: Family origin a bit of a come-down?

definitions.meaning: a downward movement or slope, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone's ancestry turns out somewhat disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or lineage, and also a downward movement or slope.
